title: Validate and tune adaptive compact Body rig segmentation for curved creatures
description:
## Summary
The compact anatomical Body rig must be density-independent without collapsing strongly curved anatomy into long straight chords. The current implementation subdivides the canonical headward and tailward spans at a fixed normalized arc step, with bounded segment counts. This task owns validation and tuning of that segmentation policy against real creatures.

## User-visible requirement
A generated creature such as `dinus_uprightus` must retain enough Body joints from pelvis through chest/neck/head and along the tail that rig manipulation follows the authored centerline rather than cutting across the mesh.

## Scope
- Validate current `AnatomicalBodyRigLayout` segmentation on real generated creatures, especially curved bodies and long tails.
- Tune segment count/placement based on canonical arc length and/or measured curvature while remaining independent of dense morphology sample count.
- Preserve stable semantic anchors (`body_pelvis`, `body_head`, `body_tail`) and deterministic indexed ordering.
- Ensure attachment-bone resolution selects the correct segment after segmentation changes.
- Ensure morphology radius bridging and skin weights remain consistent with the final segment intervals.
- Add compact-rig structural tests and generated-creature validation fixtures.

## Non-goals
- Do not restore one-bone-per-morphology-sample topology.
- Do not add biped/quadruped species modes.
- Do not replace the semantic skeleton with render-mesh-derived bones.
- Do not move locomotion or external animation-driver logic into this task.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Strongly curved Body regions contain multiple articulated segments whose rest positions remain on/near the authored centerline.
- Segment count is independent of raw Body sample count for proportional morphology.
- Head/tail canonical orientation remains correct for both stored spline directions.
- Attachments resolve to the intended segment.
- Compact Body pose tests demonstrate reduced long-segment deformation compared with the prior four-bone chord implementation.
- No regression to generation performance beyond the agreed compact-rig budget.

## Validation
Runtime/editor tests plus Unity SceneView validation on `dinus_uprightus` and at least one differently curved creature. Record segment count, attachment mapping, and controlled pose/deformation observations.

## Status
InProgress.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Created from live `dinus_uprightus` validation: the earlier compact four-bone Body topology collapsed curved chest/neck/tail geometry into long chords. Current branch retains multiple density-independent segments; this task owns validation/tuning of the final adaptive density policy rather than reverting to one-bone-per-sample.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Adversarial review found `EvaluateStored` and `EvaluateRadiusCanonical` guarded division using absolute `endT > EpsilonSqr` rather than the actual span `endT - startT`. The implementation now checks the segment span explicitly, preventing a near-zero arc interval from being divided by despite having a large absolute endpoint. This is a hardening change only; normal valid intervals produce identical results.
